title: Why sound travels faster in water than in air
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Is sound faster in water or air?
Why does sound travel faster in solids?
Why is it hard to tell where sounds come from underwater?

explain.say: Sound is a wave of pushes passed from particle to particle. How fast it travels depends on what it travels through.

draw.text: Why sound travels faster in water than in air

explain.say: In air the particles are far apart and easy to squash, so pushes pass along slowly, at about 343 metres per second.

In water the particles are packed close and water strongly resists being squashed, so each push is passed on quickly. Sound races through water at about 1,480 metres per second, more than four times faster.
In stiff solids like rock, sound is faster still, about 6,000 metres per second in granite. That is why you can hear a distant train by putting your ear to the rail, though never try it.

faq.q: Is sound faster in water or air?
faq.a: Sound travels more than four times faster in water, about 1,480 metres per second, than in air, about 343 metres per second.
asks: Does sound go faster in water?

faq.q: Why does sound travel faster in water than in air?
faq.a: Water particles are packed tightly and water is very hard to squash, so a push on one particle is passed to the next almost immediately. Air is easy to squash, so pushes travel more slowly.
asks: Why is sound faster in liquids?

faq.q: Why does sound travel faster in solids?
faq.a: Solids are stiff: their particles are tightly linked, so a vibration is passed on very quickly. In rock or steel, sound can travel around 5,000 to 6,000 metres per second.
asks: How fast is sound in steel?

faq.q: Why is it hard to tell where sounds come from underwater?
faq.a: We find a sound's direction by the tiny time gap between it reaching each ear. Underwater, sound is so fast that the gap almost disappears, so sounds seem to come from everywhere.
asks: Why can't divers tell where a sound is from?
Why do sounds seem to come from everywhere underwater?

faq.a: No. Sound needs particles to pass on its pushes, and space is almost empty. That is why space is silent.
asks: Why can't sound travel in a vacuum?

facts: Sound travels at about 343 metres per second in air at 20 degrees Celsius and about 1,480 metres per second in fresh water.
In hard rock such as granite, sound travels at roughly 5,000 to 6,000 metres per second.

quiz.say: Why does sound travel faster through water than through air?
quiz.show: Sound is faster in water because…

options.show: Water particles are close and hard to squash, so pushes pass quickly
options.say: Water particles are close and hard to squash, so pushes pass quickly

options.show: Water is always warmer than air
options.say: Water is always warmer than air

quiz.why: Water resists being squashed and its particles are packed close, so each push passes along much faster than in air.

wrong.0: Wetness has nothing to do with the speed of sound.
wrong.2: Sea water is often colder than air, yet sound is still faster in it.
